meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: AI-powered video and image generation software (text-to-video, image-to-video, generative creative tools)

analysis.summary: Little new content this month. Only Pika and HeyGen published, two pages each. Runway, Luma AI and Kling AI published nothing new.

points.text: Pika is showing customer proof from its API users, aimed at developers and builders who might buy access.
HeyGen is publishing original research on avatars and AI video, a different play from product news.
Runway has 348 pages but no new or updated pages in 30 days, while rivals are quiet too.

Runway.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days, despite a large 348-page site.

Pika.play: Posts a blog and API Club member spotlights to show customers using its tools.

Luma AI.play: Small 22-page site with no activity in 30 days.

Kling AI.play: No pages found on the site in the data.

HeyGen.play: Publishes research on AI video and avatars, plus 130 templated /tool/ pages.

shared.title: Quiet month
shared.text: Runway, Luma AI and Kling AI had no new or updated pages. Pika and HeyGen added only two each, which is too few to call a strategy.

gaps.title: Filmmaker case studies
gaps.text: Pika has only one customer-story page, aimed at API users. Nobody shows production teams using AI video in real projects.

gaps.title: Original research for creators
gaps.text: HeyGen's research covers avatars and small business. Nobody publishes data on AI video use in film or creative production.

gaps.title: Refreshed guides and updates
gaps.text: No company updated older pages this month. Runway could refresh its 348 pages and own up-to-date how-to content.
